events.text: Area acquired by Bohemia under Duke Soběslav I.

evidence.quote: The area had originally been part of the County of Kłodzko , acquired by Bohemia under Duke Soběslav I in 1137

events.label: founding
events.text: Village probably founded by Benedictine monks from Police.

evidence.quote: Sokołowsko was probably founded about 1250 by monks of the Benedictine Order

events.label: first record
events.text: Village first documented, in a deed listing villages of Radosno castle.

evidence.quote: The first record of Girbrechtsdorff is documented in a 1357 deed

events.text: Area fell to the Habsburg Monarchy with the Bohemian kingdom.

evidence.quote: With the Bohemian kingdom the area fell to the Habsburg Monarchy in 1526

events.text: Area seized by Prussia in the First Silesian War.

evidence.quote: was seized by Prussia under King Frederick II in the First Silesian War of 1742

events.text: Görbersdorf became part of the Prussian Province of Silesia.

evidence.quote: From 1815 Görbersdorf was part of the Prussian Province of Silesia

events.label: visit
events.text: Countess Maria von Colomb visited Görbersdorf and proposed a health resort.

evidence.quote: until it was visited in 1849 by Countess Maria von Colomb

events.text: Opened the world's first tuberculosis sanatorium at Görbersdorf.

evidence.quote: In 1854 she and Brehmer opened the worlds first sanatorium for the treatment of tuberculosis at Görbersdorf

events.text: Ski jumping hill opened at Görbersdorf.

evidence.quote: a ski jumping hill was opened in 1930

events.text: Görbersdorf renamed Sokołowsko, after Alfred Sokołowski.

evidence.quote: In 1945 Görbersdorf , now belonging to Poland , was named Sokołowsko

events.text: Village came under Polish administration and became part of Poland.

evidence.quote: In 1945 Görbersdorf , now belonging to Poland , was named Sokołowsko
